SddExecute.keywords: sdd, execute, ticket, phase, worker, audit
SddExecute.Mission: Execute operator-approved tickets from ticket, Execution Log, Git, and current tool output. Resolve the queue mechanically, dispatch bounded phase workers, record plan-versus-fact in each ticket's Execution Log, run real declared gates, then fresh audit and code-review. Never use a persistent SDD session, worker checkpoint JSON, retained worker identity, or scaffold-plan state.
SddExecute.BeliefState:
Inherited from the loading directive (already in context): ARTIFACT_APPROVAL_MARKER, AX_STATELESS_FLOW, AX_TOOL_INVOCATION, QUESTION_RULE_SLIM
Orchestrator owns artifact, applies edits. Critic is sensor — reports only, never edits.
Phases within one ticket dispatch strictly sequentially, in the order declared by each phase's `Deps` — a phase starts only after every phase it depends on reaches `[x] DONE` in the current Round. Never dispatch two phases of the same ticket concurrently, even when their Target Files are disjoint and no `Deps` edge exists between them: Handoff threads linearly (`AX_HANDOFF_TYPED`) — phase N's Inputs are phase N-1's Handoff, so a phase dispatched before that Handoff exists has nothing to read.
Parallelism, where available, is only across separate tickets whose Target-File sets are disjoint (`AX_DAG_AND_TICKET_BOUNDARIES`) — never within one ticket's own phases.
**Scaffolding writes a MINIMAL skeleton; phase-subagent appends event lines as work happens.**
- **SKELETON** for Round 1 = under `### Round 1 — , initial`, one `#### P` block per phase declared in Phases Overview. It contains only semantic closing placeholders; successful STEP_5 inserts its structured receipt atomically: ``` #### P - [ ] `` DONE ``` No pre-filled `file` / `test` / `cov` / `rules` / `recon` / `sync` lines — those were noise (duplicated Target Files / Test Scenario Coverage / Rules: list / git diff). Event lines (`intro` / `decision` / `tried` / `discovery` / `insight` / `verified` / `BLOCKED`) are APPENDED by the phase agent only when the event actually happens. - **FACT** = after the CLI receipt exists and the orchestrator validates the returned Handoff, `sdd-log complete --phase P` atomically replaces that current phase's closing placeholders with the timestamped `[x] DONE` + typed Handoff and sets only its `Phases Overview` status to `[x]`. A worker never performs this transition manually. Preceding event lines exist only if their event happened. - Each phase block ends with `**Handoff →** artifacts: [...]; decisions: [...]; open: [...]` line. - Round closes with `#### Round close` block (single `DONE`) emitted by orchestrator after the last phase. - **Forbidden**: `[x]` line containing any unreplaced `<…>` literal = fabricated done. - Append-only by Rounds.
A trivial phase has one CLI-owned receipt, `DONE`, and Handoff. Event lines exist only when they carry information that is not elsewhere.
Phase cannot emit Handoff without one successful `sdd-verify --task --phase `. The CLI, not the phase agent, structurally selects and runs the ladder plus every applicable ticket §5 command verbatim, then atomically writes their exact command/role/exit evidence and Target File state as the phase receipt. Any failure writes no reusable receipt and keeps the phase `[~] IN_PROGRESS` until resolved or escalated.
**MANDATORY (PROTOCOL) — Canonical Gate Rule:** Ticket §5 commands are CANONICAL and CANNOT be substituted. Diagnostics may run while fixing, but only the canonical phase command can create completion evidence; a hand-written `ver` line is not evidence.
The canon covers the script's BODY, not just its name in §5. Editing what a §5 script actually runs (e.g. rewriting `"typecheck"` in `package.json` so it does less, or points elsewhere) while logging the unchanged §5 command name is the same violation — the command stayed canonical on paper while its behavior was substituted underneath it. The one exception: `package.json` (or the script body) is itself among this phase's Target Files AND the change to that script IS the phase's stated Objective (a `bootstrap` / `config` phase whose job is exactly to define or rewire the script) — then the edit is legitimate work, not a gate dodge, and MUST be recorded as its own decision line in the Execution Log (` decision rewritten ← `) before the gate runs.
`sdd-verify --task --phase ` is NOT supplemental — it owns STEP_5, including §5 extras (see `AX_PERMITTED_BASH_COMMANDS`). §5 therefore holds only EXTRA commands beyond the standard ladder and never repeats `sdd-verify`.
Phase kind `doc` typically has no verification — empty section is acceptable.
A stop is evidence, not an automatic operator pause. Classify before routing: - `RECOVERABLE_TECHNICAL`: missing rules/config/packages, malformed task structure, gate/tool diagnostics, or audit mismatch — checkpoint, bounded replan, recheck, redispatch. - `SPEC_GOAL_CONFLICT`: repair contradicts approved spec/BDD — operator product decision. - `EXTERNAL_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED`: exact unavailable permission/authority — operator boundary. - `TECHNICAL_REPLAN_EXHAUSTED`: CLI-owned retry budget consumed — operator receives evidence.
End every phase block with a typed Handoff line consumed by the next phase and the orchestrator. Format per `HANDOFF_FORMAT`. Free-form text forbidden — the next phase reads keys, not narrative.
Tasks critiqued in DAG layers. Same layer (no inter-dependencies) → parallel dispatch. Different layers → sequential.

Contracts.Contract:
Compact, typed, single line at end of phase block: ``` **Handoff →** artifacts: [path1, path2]; decisions: [key=value, key=value]; open: [id: text, id: text]; deviations: [id: text, id: text] ``` Fields: - `artifacts` — files produced or modified by this phase (paths). - `decisions` — key facts the next phase or audit needs (e.g. `IdempotencyKey=introduced`, `module-system=esm`). - `open` — unresolved questions / risks / deferred sub-tasks (id + one-line). Empty list → `[]`. - `deviations` — spec/ticket holes this phase self-resolved rather than asking the operator (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`); each entry cites the ticket-local Decision Log id it produced (e.g. `TSK-58-D-2: chose retry cap 3, spec silent on it`). Empty list → `[]`.
Free-form text forbidden. Each field is an array (possibly empty).

Emitted by orchestrator after the LAST phase of a Round. Phase agent does NOT write this block. Tracker sync is orchestrator's mechanical work — no `sync` log line (the work happens, not informationally noteworthy). ```markdown #### Round close - [x] `` DONE ```

Final operator summary once audit settles. Plain, scannable:
📊 Task `` — Execute + Audit 🔧 Round 1: `P1 (impl, sonnet) ✅` · `P2 (test, haiku) ✅` · … 🔍 Round 1 audit: `✅ PASS` | `❌ FAIL (🔴 N · 🟠 M)` 🔄 Round 2 (if any): `P2 (fix) ✅` · audit R2 `✅` 📊 Final: `✅ PASS` | `⚠️ PASS_WITH_ACKNOWLEDGED_RISKS` | `❌ FAIL` ⏱️ wall total · 📍 files touched · ⚠️ problems encountered
If the run self-resolved any spec/ticket hole (`AX_DEVIATION_SELF_RESOLVE`), one more line before the batched `AskUserQuestion`: 🧭 Deviations: `-DL-N — ` · `-DL-M — ` · … No deviations → omit the line entirely, no batched question fires.

A disputed autonomous decision is one durable line carrying what, why, and where. Record it once in the artifact owner that a fresh agent already reads; never create a deviation sidecar or copy the same fact into both logs.
- Spec authoring or architecture: append one canonical Decision Log entry: `-DL-N — ; где: (почему: )`. - Task decomposition: append that same Decision Log grammar to the narrowest owning task index. - Phase execution: put ` ← @ ` in the current phase Handoff `deviations: [...]` field; `sdd-log complete` persists that Handoff line in the Execution Log.
Obvious/recoverable mechanics are not deviations. Record only a choice a fresh agent could not re-derive from artifacts. Uncertainty does not pause an autonomous batch: record the smallest safe choice and continue. Operator review happens once, after the whole batch and its audits.

SddExecute.HaltConditions: | ID | Trigger | |---|---| | `H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK` | Empty/ambiguous selection cannot identify one intended ticket set | | `H_TICKET_NOT_APPROVED` | Owning index lacks a current approval #2 marker or current Git/artifact evidence makes it semantically stale | | `H_PHASE_BLOCKED` | Worker names a concrete missing external decision/capability after bounded diagnosis | | `H_REAL_GATE_RED` | A declared real verification command remains red after one evidence-based correction | | `H_REQUIREMENT_UNCOVERED` | A mandatory Requirement-ID is absent from implemented tests |

Step.Goal: Select tickets from the deterministic execution map.
Step.Action:
Resolve the operator selector with exact tool output, not repository archaeology. npx gennady sdd-task
Consume `executionMap`. Empty payload: show pickable Task-ID/path rows and wait. `next`/`pick`: proceed only when the map identifies exactly one pickable ticket; otherwise ask for explicit selection and stop with `H_AMBIGUOUS_TASK` if one intended set still cannot be identified. A concrete Task-ID resolves only that ticket. `all`/`batch`/`queue` uses every pickable ticket in DAG order per `AX_EXECUTION_ORDER`. Per `AX_TASK_PARALLEL`, parallelize only tickets with disjoint target files and no dependency relation; otherwise serialize. Model session identity is irrelevant to correctness.

For each selected ticket call the canonical resolver and consume its exact paths, phase state, spec references, dependency state, and verification declarations. npx gennady sdd-task <ticket>
Consume `taskMap`, then read only the ticket, referenced spec anchors, declared rules, current Execution Log, and relevant Git diff/status. Require a well-formed `approved` approval #2 marker in the owning task index that lists the selected ticket. Mechanics check its shape and membership; use semantic judgment over current artifacts and Git evidence for staleness, never a content hash. Missing, malformed, or semantically stale approval stops with `H_TICKET_NOT_APPROVED`. A completed phase is trusted only when its Execution Log fact and repository evidence agree. Resume from the first incomplete/invalid phase. Do not infer progress from agent memory or hidden scratch state (`AX_STATELESS_FLOW`). The ticket/index ownership boundary remains authoritative per `AX_OWNER`.

Step.Goal: Check phase coherence and expose the immediate plan.
Step.Action: Mentally simulate the declared phases against their dependencies, targets, requirements, and verification commands. Confirm providers precede consumers and every phase has an observable completion condition. If the ticket itself is inconsistent, stop and return it to scaffold; do not invent a replacement plan in JSON. Show the concise phase sequence and start.

Step.Goal: Execute one declared phase through one bounded worker.
Step.Action:
Load `phase-execution-protocol.directive.xml`, then obtain the canonical worker context: npx gennady sdd-task <ticket> --phase <PhaseID> Dispatch a fresh worker with the complete `phaseContext` output verbatim as the leading prompt block, followed by exact resolved spec/rule excerpts and current Git evidence. Never summarize, retype, or omit its lifecycle manifest and worker contract. The worker edits only its declared targets, runs the phase's real verification, and returns a typed handoff. Apart from the receipt written by `sdd-verify`, the worker never edits the ticket or invokes `sdd-log`.
Evaluate the typed handoff per `AX_HANDOFF_TYPED` against repository evidence. Per `AX_HALT_VS_FAIL_DISTINCTION`, on a recoverable technical failure form one new concrete hypothesis, correct the phase within its approved boundary, and redispatch a fresh bounded worker. Do not require continuation of the same worker and do not serialize a checkpoint. A change to task meaning, dependencies, phases, or test plan invalidates approval #2 and returns to scaffold. A concrete missing external decision or capability that remains after bounded diagnosis stops with `H_PHASE_BLOCKED`.

Step.Goal: Prove the phase's task-visible mechanics, then atomically close it before any dependent dispatch.
Step.Action:
After the worker returns, verify its typed Handoff against Git, the declared Target Files, and the successful CLI-owned receipt. Before closing the phase, run the ticket's mechanical check against the worker's actual files: npx gennady sdd-check --task <ticket> Consume `preCloseTaskGate`. Existing future test files may still be absent, but any file this worker created is checked immediately against its canonical Test Scenario Coverage names. A red result is `RECOVERABLE_TECHNICAL`: correct and re-verify while the phase is still unchecked; never persist DONE/Handoff for evidence already known to be inconsistent.
Only after that gate is green, perform exactly one structural transition owned by this step: npx gennady sdd-log <ticket> complete "<handoff payload>" --phase <PhaseID>
Consume `phaseClose` per `AX_EXECUTION_LOG_PLAN_VS_FACT`. Success means the current phase's skeleton DONE and Handoff placeholders were replaced with facts and only that phase's `Phases Overview` status became `[x]`. Failure keeps the phase incomplete and is handled as `RECOVERABLE_TECHNICAL`; never dispatch a dependent phase and never inspect CLI source to guess how to repair the state. Commands and exact exit evidence remain in the CLI-owned receipt; do not duplicate them as prose. Commit boundaries follow repository policy. The Execution Log plus Git is sufficient for a fresh orchestrator to continue; no worker ID or hidden NEXT token is recorded. When the phase made a disputed autonomous choice, its typed Handoff carries one `deviations: [ ← @ ]` value per `DEVIATION_RECORD_FORMAT`; `phaseClose` persists it in the existing Execution Log rather than a second journal.

Step.Goal: Prove the implemented ticket, then make ticket and tracker state coherent before audit.
Step.Action:
Per `AX_VERIFICATION_BEFORE_HANDOFF`, after all phases confirm the durable post-transition ticket state with the mechanical task check. Exact verification commands were already owned by each phase receipt and MUST NOT be run again here. Never replace real test/type/lint/coverage output with reviewer prose. npx gennady sdd-check --task <ticket>
Consume `taskGate`. The mechanical check must prove that every mandatory Requirement-ID appears in an implemented test and maps to a declared scenario; happy-path-only coverage is invalid when the ticket/spec requires negative/failure behavior. Semantic judgment remains responsible for whether the assertion actually demonstrates the requirement, but missing IDs or mappings stop with `H_REQUIREMENT_UNCOVERED`. If a declared real gate remains red after one evidence-based correction, stop with `H_REAL_GATE_RED`.
Once `taskGate` is green, close the current Round and synchronize the resulting ticket status into its owning task indexes before any audit reads the group: npx gennady sdd-log <ticket> close npx gennady sdd-sync <ticket> npx gennady sdd-check --all . Consume all three results. `roundClose` replaces the scaffolded Round-close skeleton exactly once; never edit or delete that block manually. `trackerSync` is required even for a single ticket. A red `coherentTreeGate` is corrected before audit, so audit never receives a known ticket/index status drift as an implementation finding.

Dispatch a fresh `sdd-audit` over the completed sibling group, then a fresh `sdd-code-review` after audit passes. Audit checks spec/ticket/diff/log agreement. Code-review hunts behavioral bugs, negative paths, error handling, security, and concurrency. Neither role depends on or receives a saved session glossary or worker history.
Findings route to the owning artifact: code bug reopens the ticket; spec contradiction returns to spec authoring and approval #1; decomposition/test-plan change returns to scaffold and approval #2. Rerun affected real gates after correction.

Step.Goal: Close the ticket group and choose the next durable queue item.
Step.Action: The ticket and trackers were already transitioned to coherent DONE state in STEP_5 so audit could inspect the actual final artifact graph. Do not repeat `sdd-log close` or `sdd-sync`. Emit the execute summary from actual tool results. For batch mode, refresh the execution map. npx gennady sdd-task Consume `refreshedExecutionMap` and continue with the next pickable ticket. Otherwise show the next concrete Task-ID/path or state that the queue is complete. In batch mode only, once the queue is complete after all selected tickets and audits, dynamically `READ_AND_USE_DIRECTIVE("ai/directives/sdd-v2/deviation-review.directive.xml")`. Never pause for this review between tickets. No session close operation exists.
